Contemporary Sesame Broccoli and Bell Pepper Salad

Blanched broccoli and raw bell pepper in a toasted-sesame dressing is this list's modern build — no old papers, just the namul family's method (#B06) applied to the vegetables the contemporary table actually keeps in the fridge.

Korean · Easy · Serves 4 as banchan

Behind the dish

A PLACE AT
the table.

Stream: contemporary — the modern table's crunch. Blanched broccoli and raw bell pepper in a toasted-sesame dressing is this list's modern build — no old papers, just the namul family's method (#B06) applied to the vegetables the contemporary table actually keeps in the fridge. It keeps in the refrigerator for days where the lettuce bowls (#F03) last an hour, which is exactly why it exists: the grill night's make-ahead bowl.

The vegetables

Set yourself up

Before you cook

  • Blanch the broccoli hard-and-short: 90 seconds in rolling unsalted water, straight to ice water — the #F04 law of vivid-green-and-firm. The florets should come out brighter than they went in and stop a shade short of fully tender (the dressing's minute finishes them).
  • Cut the pepper batons to match the florets' scale — one bowl, one bite-size; the geometry is the toss.

LET’S make it.

  1. 01
    The blanched, dried broccoli and the raw pepper in the serving bowl, the dressing poured over — sesame oil, soy, honey, garlic — and tossed with spoons for thirty seconds. Checkpoint — every floret glossed, the sesame seeds caught in the florets' crowns (the flat-top cut's doing), the pepper's raw crunch intact beside the broccoli's blanched-firm.
  2. 02
    Scallion and gochugaru over, one more turn, and the bowl either serves now or lides and chills. Checkpoint — the eating test: sesame-forward, the broccoli's green sweetness, the pepper's bright crunch — a bowl that tastes like the modern Korean lunch café's cold-case, which is precisely its lineage and its honest seat at this grill table. Chef’s Note — this bowl earns its place by logistics rather than tradition: every other fresh record on this list eats within the hour, and the grill night planned a day ahead needs one vegetable bowl that does not. Blanched broccoli holds its snap under dressing for two days — the floret's structure is the reason — and this salad is the answer to the Thursday-prepared, Saturday-grilled table. Labeled modern, filed under useful.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Broccoli olive-drabOver-blanched, slow shock90 seconds; ice water waiting
Florets mushy under dressingBlanched to done, not short-ofPull a shade early; the toss finishes
Bowl watery next dayWet florets at dressingDry the ice bath off completely
Pepper wept into the bowlSalted or dressed too longRaw pepper, undressed until serving for day-two service

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

  • The make-ahead exception: keeps 2 days refrigerated, the Florets holding snap — refresh with a few drops of sesame oil and a re-toss at serving.
  • Variations: blanched green beans for broccoli; matchstick carrot for pepper; a spoon of cho-gochujang (#SA03) swirled into the dressing for the sweet-heat fork.
